terms.gloss: a board, a plank; in the plural, floorboards
evidence: Vitr. 7.1.2: nē commisceantur axēs aesculīnī quercō
Plin. NH 36.187: pavīmentum quernīs axibus (Lewis & Short s.v. contabulō)
terms.comment: The same word as axis, axle, in its builder’s sense (also written assis); Vitruvius uses it of the boards of a floor. For a single board, tabula will do (see “board”).

evidence: Vitr. 7.1.5: Cum coaxātum fuerit, super altera coaxātiō trānsversa sternātur
terms.comment: Vitruvius’s word for the boarding as a whole (Lewis & Short coassātiō, also coax-).

phrases.english: The floorboards creak when you walk on them.

phrases.latin: Item danda est opera, nē commisceantur axēs aesculīnī quercō, quod quercei, simul ūmōrem percēpērunt, sē torquentēs rīmās faciunt in pavīmentīs.
phrases.english: Care must also be taken not to mix boards of Italian oak with common oak, because the oak ones, as soon as they take in moisture, warp and open cracks in the floors.

sources: Lewis & Short: axis · Lewis & Short: coassatio · Lewis & Short: contabulo
